docs.ENCODER_HALL_PHASE_CALIBRATION: Rotate the motor for 30s to calibrate hall sensor edge offsets
docs.ENCODER_HALL_POLARITY_CALIBRATION: Rotate the motor in lockin and calibrate hall polarity
docs.ENCODER_INDEX_SEARCH: Turn the motor in one direction until the encoder index is traversed.
docs.ENCODER_OFFSET_CALIBRATION: Turn the motor in one direction for a few seconds and then back to measure the offset between the encoder position and the electrical phase.
docs.FULL_CALIBRATION_SEQUENCE: Run motor calibration and then encoder offset calibration (or encoder index search if `<axis>.encoder.config.use_index` is `True`).
docs.IDLE: Disable motor PWM and do nothing.
docs.MOTOR_CALIBRATION: Measure phase resistance and phase inductance of the motor.

docs.ESTOP_REQUESTED: The estop message was sent over CAN
docs.HOMING_WITHOUT_ENDSTOP: the min endstop was not enabled during homing
docs.UNKNOWN_POSITION: There isn't a valid position estimate available.

docs.SIMPLE: CANSimple, an ODrive-specific protocol for basic functionality

docs.POSITION_CONTROL:
Uses the inner torque loop, the velocity control loop, and the outer position control loop.
Use `input_pos` to command desired position, `input_vel` to command velocity feed-forward, and `input_torque` for torque feed-forward.
docs.TORQUE_CONTROL:
Uses only the inner torque control loop.
Use `input_torque` to command desired torque.
Note the setting `motor.config.torque_constant`.
Note the setting `enable_torque_mode_vel_limit`.
docs.VELOCITY_CONTROL:
Uses both the inner torque control loop and the velocity control loop.
Use `input_vel` to command desired velocity, and `input_torque`.
docs.VOLTAGE_CONTROL: Note: This mode is not used internally.  For voltage-only FOC, use `MotorType.GIMBAL`

docs.INVALID_CIRCULAR_RANGE: Indicates the encoder estimation module declined to output a circular position value and the exception was caught.
docs.INVALID_ESTIMATE: Indicates the encoder estimation module declined to output a linear position or velocity value and the exception was caught.
docs.INVALID_INPUT_MODE: The `config.input_mode` setting was set to an invalid value. See InputMode for available values
docs.OVERSPEED: Motor speed exceeded `config.vel_limit * config.vel_limit_tolerance` and `config.enable_overspeed_error` was enabled.
docs.SPINOUT_DETECTED:
The motor mechanical power and electrical power do not agree. This is usually
caused by a slipping encoder or incorrect encoder offset calibration.
Check that your encoder is not slipping on the motor. If using an Index pin, check
that you are not getting false index pulses caused by noise. This can happen if you
are using unshielded cable for the encoder signals.
docs.UNSTABLE_GAIN: `motor.config.bandwidth` was set too high to create a stable controller.

docs.INACTIVE: Disable inputs. Setpoints retain their last value.
docs.POS_FILTER: Implements a 2nd order position tracking filter.
docs.TORQUE_RAMP: Ramp a torque command from the current value to the target value.
docs.TRAP_TRAJ: Implementes an online trapezoidal trajectory planner.
docs.VEL_RAMP: Ramps a velocity command from the current value to the target value.

docs.CPR_POLEPAIRS_MISMATCH:
Confirm you have entered the correct count per rotation (CPR) for
[your encoder](https://docs.odriverobotics.com/encoders). The
ODrive uses your supplied value for the motor pole pairs to
measure the CPR. So you should also double check this value.

If you are still having issues, you can try to increase
`config.calib_scan_distance` up to a factor of 4 above the default.

If your encoder cpr and motor pole pair settings are correct,
this error can be caused because motor cogging makes the motor
move less or more than commanded. You can fix this by increasing
`config.calib_scan_distance`.

Note that the AMT encoders are configurable using the micro-
switches on the encoder PCB and so you may need to check that
these are in the right positions. If your encoder lists its pulse
per rotation (PPR) multiply that number by four to get CPR.
docs.ILLEGAL_HALL_STATE:
Hall effect encoder only have 6 valid states out of 8 (2^3) possible states.
An invalid state can be caused by noise or a hardware fault. If you get this
error and you are sure that your electrical connections are correct, add
22nF capacitors between the encoder A,B,Z pins and ground to filter out noise.
docs.INDEX_NOT_FOUND_YET:
Check that your encoder is a model that has an index pulse. If
your encoder does not have a wire connected to pin Z on your
ODrive then it does not output an index pulse.
docs.NO_RESPONSE:
Confirm that your encoder is plugged into the right pins on the
ODrive board.

docs.SPI_ABS_AMS: Compatible with AMS AS5047P, AS5048A/AS5048B (no daisy chain support)

docs.CONTROL_ITERATION_MISSED: At least one control iteration was missed.
docs.DC_BUS_OVER_CURRENT: Too much current was pulled from the power supply. `ibus` exceeded `config.dc_max_positive_current`.
docs.DC_BUS_OVER_REGEN_CURRENT:
Current flowing back into the power supply exceeded `config.dc_max_negative_current`.
This can happen if your brake resistor is disabled or unable to handle the braking current.

Check that `config.enable_brake_resistor` is `True` and that
`(V_power_supply / Brake_resistance) > (total motor.config.current_lim + total motor.config.current_lim_margin)`.
docs.DC_BUS_OVER_VOLTAGE: The DC voltage exceeded the limit configured in `config.dc_bus_overvoltage_trip_level`.
docs.DC_BUS_UNDER_VOLTAGE: The DC voltage fell below the limit configured in `config.dc_bus_undervoltage_trip_level`.
docs.INVALID_BRAKE_RESISTANCE: `config.brake_resistance` is non-positive or NaN. Make sure that `config.brake_resistance` is a positive number.

docs.ANALOG_IN:
The pin can be used for one or more of these functions:
Sin/cos encoders, analog input, `get_adc_voltage()`.
docs.DIGITAL:
The pin can be used for one or more of these functions:
Step, dir, enable, encoder index, hall effect encoder, SPI encoder nCS (this one is exclusive).
docs.DIGITAL_PULL_DOWN: Same as `DIGITAL` but with the internal pull-down resistor enabled.
docs.DIGITAL_PULL_UP: Same as `DIGITAL` but with the internal pull-up resistor enabled.
docs.ENC0: The pin is used by quadrature encoder 0.
docs.ENC1: The pin is used by quadrature encoder 1.
docs.ENC2: This mode is not supported on ODrive v3.x.
docs.MECH_BRAKE: This is to support external mechanical brakes.
docs.SPI_A: Note that the SPI pins on ODrive v3.x are hardwired so they cannot be configured through software. Consequently
docs.STATUS: The pin is used for status output (see `config.error_gpio_pin`)
docs.UART_B: This mode is not supported on ODrive v3.x.
docs.UART_C: This mode is not supported on ODrive v3.x.

docs.BAD_TIMING: The main control loop got out of sync with the motor control loop. This could indicate that the main control loop got stuck.
docs.BRAKE_RESISTOR_DISARMED:
An attempt was made to run the motor PWM while the brake resistor was configured as enabled
(`config.enable_brake_resistor`) but disarmed.

The most common cause is that you just set `config.enable_brake_resistor` to `True` but didn't
arm the brake resistor yet (by either rebooting or running `odrvX.clear_errors()`).

Otherwise, the brake resistor can be disarmed due to various system-wide errors.
The root cause will usually show up under `system` when you run `dump_errors(odrvX)`.

To re-arm the brake resistor reboot the ODrive or run `odrvX.clear_errors()`.
docs.CONTROLLER_FAILED: The motor was disarmed because the underlying controller failed. Usually this is the FOC controller.
docs.CONTROLLER_INITIALIZING: Internal value used while the controller is not yet ready to generate PWM timings.
docs.CURRENT_LIMIT_VIOLATION:
The motor current exceeded `motor.config.current_lim + motor.config.current_lim_margin`.
The current controller is a PI controller, so it can experience overshoot. The PI gains
are automatically calculated based on `config.current_control_bandwidth` and the
motor resistance and inductance (pole placement). Some overshoot is normal, so a sensible
solution is to increase the current limit margin if your current limit is large.
docs.CURRENT_MEASUREMENT_UNAVAILABLE: The phase current measurement is not available. The ADC failed to sample the current sensor in time. This is not expected in official release firmware.
docs.CURRENT_SENSE_SATURATION:
The current sense circuit saturated the current sense amplifier.
This can be caused by setting `config.current_lim` higher than
`config.requested_current_range`. If this happens, increase the
requested current range, save the configuration, and reboot the controller.
docs.DRV_FAULT: The gate driver chip reported an error.
docs.FET_THERMISTOR_OVER_TEMP: The inverter thermistor measured a temperature above motor.fet_thermistor.config.temp_limit_upper
docs.I_BUS_OUT_OF_RANGE:
The DC current sourced/sunk by this motor exceeded the configured
hard limits. More specifically `I_bus` fell outside of the range
`config.I_bus_hard_min` ... `config.I_bus_hard_max`.
docs.MODULATION_MAGNITUDE:
The bus voltage was insufficent to push the requested current
through the motor.
If you are getting this during motor calibration, make sure that
`config.resistance_calib_max_voltage` is no more than half
your bus voltage.

For gimbal motors, it is recommended to set the
`config.calibration_current` and `config.current_lim`
to half your bus voltage, or less.
docs.MOTOR_THERMISTOR_OVER_TEMP: The motor thermistor measured a temperature above motor.motor_thermistor.config.temp_limit_upper
docs.PHASE_INDUCTANCE_OUT_OF_RANGE: The measured motor phase inductance is outside of the plausible range.
docs.PHASE_RESISTANCE_OUT_OF_RANGE: The measured motor phase resistance is outside of the plausible range.
docs.SYSTEM_LEVEL:
The motor had to be disarmed because of a system level error.
See `ODrive:error` for more details.
docs.TIMER_UPDATE_MISSED: A timer update event was missed. Perhaps the previous timer update took too much time. This is not expected in official release firmware.
docs.UNBALANCED_PHASES: The motor phases are not balanced.
docs.UNKNOWN_CURRENT_COMMAND: The current controller did not get a valid current setpoint. Maybe you didn't configure the controller correctly.
docs.UNKNOWN_CURRENT_MEASUREMENT: The current controller did not get a valid current measurement.
docs.UNKNOWN_GAINS: The current controller gains were not configured. Run motor calibration or set `config.phase_resistance` and `config.phase_inductance` manually.
docs.UNKNOWN_PHASE_ESTIMATE: The current controller did not get a valid angle input. Maybe you didn't calibrate the encoder.
docs.UNKNOWN_PHASE_VEL: The motor controller did not get a valid phase velocity input.
docs.UNKNOWN_TORQUE: The motor controller did not get a valid torque input.
docs.UNKNOWN_VBUS_VOLTAGE: The current controller did not get a valid `ODrive:vbus_voltage` measurement.
docs.UNKNOWN_VOLTAGE_COMMAND: The current controller did not get a valid feedforward voltage setpoint.

docs.ACIM: Used for FOC control of AC Induction Motors (ACIM), aka Asynchronous motors,
docs.GIMBAL:
Enables voltage-only FOC where V=IR can be assumed to be correct.
Used for high-phase-resistance motors (> 1 ohm), which are typically sold as "Gimbal" motors.
docs.HIGH_CURRENT:
Used for all standard "hobby-style" motors Permanant Magnet AC (PMAC) or Brushless DC (BLDC) motors.  This is the default.
Note: Assumes sinusoidal back-EMF, "wye" connected motors.  Trapezoidal bEMF may have reduced controllability.

docs.ASCII:
Human readable protocol designed for easy implementation for cases
where the use of libfibre is not desired or feasible.
Refer to [this page](ascii-protocol.md) for details.
docs.FIBRE:
Machine-to-machine protocol which gives access to all features of the
ODrive. This protocol is used by the official odrivetool and GUI.
Developers who wish to interact with this protocol are advised to do
so through libfibre.
docs.STDOUT: Output of printf(). Only intended for developers who modify ODrive firmware.

axis0.controller.move_incremental.doc: Moves the axes' goal point by a specified increment.

in.doc: If true, the increment is applied relative to `input_pos`. If false, the increment is applied relative to `pos_setpoint`, which usually corresponds roughly to the current position of the axis.
in.name: from_input_pos

axis0.mechanical_brake.engage.doc: This function engages the mechanical brake if one is present and enabled.

axis0.mechanical_brake.release.doc: This function releases the mecahncal brake if one is present and enabled.

axis0.watchdog_feed.doc: Feed the watchdog to prevent watchdog timeouts.

axis1.controller.move_incremental.doc: Moves the axes' goal point by a specified increment.

in.doc: If true, the increment is applied relative to `input_pos`. If false, the increment is applied relative to `pos_setpoint`, which usually corresponds roughly to the current position of the axis.
in.name: from_input_pos

axis1.mechanical_brake.engage.doc: This function engages the mechanical brake if one is present and enabled.

axis1.watchdog_feed.doc: Feed the watchdog to prevent watchdog timeouts.

clear_errors.doc: Clear all the errors of this device including all contained submodules.

enter_dfu_mode.doc: Enters the Device Firmware Update mode

erase_configuration.doc: Resets all `config` variables to their default values and reboots the controller

get_adc_voltage.doc: Reads the ADC voltage of the specified GPIO. The GPIO should be in `GPIO_MODE_ANALOG_IN`.}

get_dma_status.doc: Returns information about the specified DMA stream.

out.doc:
bit 31:     zero if the stream's configuration is equal to the reset state
bits 4:2:   channel
bits 1:0:   priority (3 is highest priority)
0xffffffff if the specified number is not a valid DMA stream number.
out.name: status

get_gpio_states.doc: Returns the logic states of all GPIOs. Bit i represents the state of GPIOi.

get_interrupt_status.doc: Returns information about the specified interrupt number.

out.doc:
bit 31:     enabled (1) or disabled (0)
bits 30:8:  number of times the interrupt fired (modulo 0x800000)
bits 7:0:   priority (0 is highest priority)
0xffffffff if the specified number is not a valid interrupt number.
out.name: status

reboot.doc: Reboots the controller without saving the current configuraiton

save_configuration.doc: Saves the current configuration to non-volatile memory and reboots the board.

axis0.acim_estimator.phase_offset.doc: estimate offset between physical and electrical angular position}

axis0.acim_estimator.rotor_flux.doc: estimated magnitude of the rotor flux

axis0.acim_estimator.slip_vel.doc: estimated slip between physical and electrical angular velocity}

axis0.acim_estimator.stator_phase.doc: calculated setpoint for the electrical phase}

axis0.acim_estimator.stator_phase_vel.doc: calculated setpoint for the electrical velocity}

axis0.config.enable_step_dir.doc:
Enable step/dir input after calibration.
Make sure to set the corresponding GPIO's mode to `GPIO_MODE_DIGITAL`.

axis0.config.startup_closed_loop_control.doc: Enable closed loop control after calibration/startup

axis0.config.startup_encoder_index_searc.doc: Run encoder index search after startup, skip otherwise this only has an effect if encoder.config.use_index is also true

axis0.config.startup_encoder_offset_cali.doc: Run encoder offset calibration after startup, skip otherwise

axis0.config.startup_motor_calibration.doc: Run motor calibration at startup, skip otherwise

axis0.config.step_dir_always_on.doc:
Keep step/dir enabled while the motor is disabled.
This is ignored if enable_step_dir is false.
This setting only takes effect on a state transition
into idle or out of closed loop control.

axis0.controller.autotuning_phase.doc: The current phase angle of the `INPUT_MODE_TUNING` sine wave generator

axis0.controller.config.axis_to_mirror.doc: The axis used for mirroring when in `INPUT_MODE_MIRROR`

axis0.controller.config.circular_setpoin.doc: circular range in [turns] for position setpoints when circular_setpoints is True

axis0.controller.config.electrical_power.doc: Bandwidth for electrical power estimate. Used for spinout detection. Dot product of Vdq and Idq

axis0.controller.config.enable_gain_sche.doc:
Enable the experimental "gain scheduling" module, which reduces the `pos_gain`, `vel_gain`, and `vel_integrator_gain` according to the position error.
Also known as "anti-hunt"

axis0.controller.config.enable_overspeed.doc: Enables the velocity controller's overspeed error

axis0.controller.config.enable_torque_mo.doc: Enable velocity limit in torque control mode (requires a valid velocity estimator).

axis0.controller.config.homing_speed.doc: The speed at which the axis moves towards the `min_endstop` during `AXIS_STATE_HOMING`

axis0.controller.config.input_filter_ban.doc: Sets the position filter's P and I gains to emulate a critically-damped 2nd order mass-spring-damper motion.

axis0.controller.config.load_encoder_axi.doc: Default depends on Axis number and is set in load_configuration()

axis0.controller.config.mechanical_power.doc: Bandwidth for mechanical power estimate. Used for spinout detection

axis0.controller.config.mirror_ratio.doc: The ratio applied to position and velocity movements of the mirrored axis.  To reverse movements, use a negative value

axis0.controller.config.spinout_electric.doc: Electrical power threshold for spinout detection. This should be a positive value

axis0.controller.config.spinout_mechanic.doc: Mechanical power threshold for spinout detection. This should be a negative value

axis0.controller.config.steps_per_circul.doc: Number of steps within the circular setpoint range. Set this and the circular setpoint range to powers of 2 for the best results.

axis0.controller.config.torque_mirror_ra.doc: The ratio applied to torque values of the mirrored axis.

axis0.controller.config.vel_integrator_l.doc: Limit the integrator output (independent of proportional gain output). Set to infinity to disable. Units = N·m

axis0.controller.input_pos.doc:
Set the desired position of the axis.  Only valid in `CONTROL_MODE_POSITION_CONTROL`.startup.
Also updates the step count.
In `INPUT_MODE_TUNING`, this acts as a DC offset for the position sine wave.

axis0.controller.input_torque.doc:
In `CONTROL_MODE_TORQUE_CONTROL`, sets the desired output torque of the axis.
In `CONTROL_MODE_VELOCITY_CONTROL` and `CONTROL_MODE_POSITION_CONTROL`, sets the feed-forward torque of the torque controller.
In `INPUT_MODE_TUNING`, this acts as a DC offset for the torque sine wave.

axis0.controller.input_vel.doc:
In `CONTROL_MODE_VELOCITY_CONTROL`, sets the desired velocity of the axis.
In `CONTROL_MODE_POSITION_CONTROL`, sets the feed-forward velocity of the velocity controller
In `INPUT_MODE_TUNING`, this acts as a DC offset for the velocity sine wave.

axis0.controller.pos_setpoint.doc: The position reference actually being used by the position controller.  This is the same as `input_pos` in `INPUT_MODE_PASSTHROUGH`, but may vary according to `InputMode`.

axis0.controller.torque_setpoint.doc: The torque reference actually being used by the torque controller.  This is the same as `input_vel` in `INPUT_MODE_PASSTHROUGH`, but may vary according to `InputMode`.

axis0.controller.trajectory_done.doc: Indicates the last commanded Trapezoidal Trajectory movement is complete.

axis0.controller.vel_integrator_torque.doc: The accumulated value of the velocity loop integrator

axis0.controller.vel_setpoint.doc: The velocity reference actually being used by the velocity controller.  This is the same as `input_vel` in `INPUT_MODE_PASSTHROUGH`, but may vary according to `InputMode`.

axis0.current_state.brief: The current state of the axis

axis0.encoder.config.abs_spi_cs_gpio_pin.doc: Make sure that the GPIO is in `GPIO_MODE_DIGITAL`.

axis0.encoder.config.calib_range.doc: The error threshold for encoder offset calibration, in turns.  If the

axis0.encoder.config.calib_scan_distance.doc:
The distance the motor is turned during encoder offset calibration.
This is in the electrical frame, so if you want a 7pp motor to turn 1 mechanical revolution, you would put `(7 * 2*pi)`

axis0.encoder.config.calib_scan_omega.doc:
The speed the motor turns during encoder offset calibration.
This is in the electrical frame, so a 7pp motor rotating 1 mechanical revolution in 2 sec would be set to `(7 * 2*pi) / 2`

axis0.encoder.config.cpr.doc: Counts per Revolution of the encoder.  This is 4x the Pulses per Revolution.

axis0.encoder.config.index_offset.doc: When the index is found, the linear position of the axis will be set to this value if `use_index_offset` is set to `True`.

axis0.encoder.config.sincos_gpio_pin_cos.doc: Analog cosine signal of a sin/cos encoder. The corresponding GPIO must be in `GPIO_MODE_ANALOG_IN`.

axis0.encoder.config.sincos_gpio_pin_sin.doc: Analog sine signal of a sin/cos encoder. The corresponding GPIO must be in `GPIO_MODE_ANALOG_IN`.

axis0.encoder.config.use_index.doc: Set this to `True` when using an encoder with an index pin to allow pre-calibration of the encoder and encoder index search.

axis0.encoder.config.use_index_offset.doc: Set this to `True` to have the axis set the linear position of the axis to `index_offset` when the index is found during encoder index search

axis0.encoder.count_in_cpr.doc: Raw circular count from the encoder on [0, cpr)

axis0.encoder.delta_pos_cpr_counts.doc: Circular position delta of the encoder in the most recent loop. Primarily for debug purposes, it indicates much the encoder changed since the last time it was checked.

axis0.encoder.pos_abs.doc: The last (valid) position from an absolute encoder, if used.

axis0.encoder.pos_circular.doc: Circular position estimate of the encoder, as a decimal from [0, 1).  Also known as "single-turn" position.

axis0.encoder.pos_cpr_counts.doc: Circular position estimate of the encoder, on the space [0, cpr).

axis0.encoder.pos_estimate.doc: Linear position estimate of the encoder, in turns.  Also known as "multi-turn" position.

axis0.encoder.pos_estimate_counts.doc: Linear position estimate of the encoder, in counts.  Equal to `pos_estimate * config.cpr`

axis0.encoder.shadow_count.doc: Raw linear count from the encoder.

axis0.encoder.vel_estimate.doc: Estimate of the linear velocity of an axis in turn/s

axis0.encoder.vel_estimate_counts.doc: Estimate of the linear velocity of an axis, in counts/s.

axis0.is_homed.brief: Whether or not the axis has been successfully homed.

axis0.max_endstop.config.gpio_num.doc: Make sure the corresponding GPIO is in `GPIO_MODE_DIGITAL`.

axis0.min_endstop.config.gpio_num.doc: Make sure the corresponding GPIO is in `GPIO_MODE_DIGITAL`.

axis0.motor.I_bus.doc: The current in the ODrive DC bus.  This is also the current seen by the power supply in most systems.

axis0.motor.config.I_bus_hard_max.doc:
If the controller fails to keep this motor's DC current (`ODrive.Motor:I_bus`)
below this value the motor gets disarmed immediately. Usually this
is set in conjunction with `I_bus_hard_min`. Set to inf to disable.
Take noise into account when chosing a value.

axis0.motor.config.I_bus_hard_min.doc:
If the controller fails to keep this motor's DC current (`ODrive.Motor:I_bus`)
above this value the motor gets disarmed immediately. Most likely
you want a negative value here. Set to -inf to disable. Take noise
into account when chosing a value.

axis0.motor.config.I_leak_max.doc:
In almost all scenarios, the currents on phase A, B and C should
add up to zero. A small amount of measurement noise is expected.
However if the sum of A, B, C currents exceeds this configuration
value, the motor gets disarmed immediately.

Note that this feature is only works on devices with three current
sensors (e.g. ODrive v4).

axis0.motor.config.R_wL_FF_enable.doc: Enables automatic feedforward of the R*wL term in the current controller.

axis0.motor.config.bEMF_FF_enable.doc: Enables automatic feedforward of the bEMF term in the current controller.

axis0.motor.config.calibration_current.doc: The current used to measure resistance during `AXIS_STATE_MOTOR_CALIBRATION`.

axis0.motor.config.current_control_bandw.doc:
Sets the PI gains of the Q and D axis FOC control according to `phase_resistance` and `phase_inductance` to create a critically-damped controller with a -3dB
bandwidth at this frequency.

axis0.motor.config.current_lim_margin.doc: Maximum measured current allowed above `current_lim`.  Any value above `current_lim + curren_lim_margin` will throw a `CURRENT_LIMIT_VIOLATION` error.

axis0.motor.config.pole_pairs.doc:
The number of pole pairs in the motor.
Note this is equal to 1/2 of the number of magnets (not coils!) in a typical hobby motor.

axis0.motor.config.pre_calibrated.doc:
Indicates to the ODrive that the parameters `config.phase_resistance` and `config.phase_inductance` are valid at system start.
If these are valid and `pre_calibrated` is set to `True`, motor calibration can be skipped.

axis0.motor.config.requested_current_ran.doc:
The minimum phase current range expected to be measured.  This is used to set the current shunt amplifier gains.
This should be set > `current_lim + curren_lim_margin`, but as low as possible to maximize precision and accuracy of the controller.

axis0.motor.config.resistance_calib_max_.doc:
The maximum voltage allowed during `AXIS_STATE_MOTOR_CALIBRATION`.
This should be set to less than `(0.5 * vbus_voltage)`, but high enough to satisfy V=IR during motor calibration, where I is `config.calibration_current` and R is `config.phase_resistance`

axis0.motor.config.torque_lim.doc: Maximum commanded torque allowed in the torque loop.

axis0.motor.current_control.Id_measured.doc: The phase current measured along the "d" axis in the FOC control loop.  This should be close to 0 for typical surface permanent magnet motors.

axis0.motor.current_control.Iq_measured.doc: The phase current measured along the "q" axis in the FOC control loop.  This is the torque-generating current, so motor torque is approx. `torque_constant * Iq_measured`

axis0.motor.current_control.power.doc: The electrical power being delivered to the motor

axis0.motor.effective_current_lim.doc: This value is the internally-limited value of phase current allowed according to the set current limit and the FET and Motor thermistor limits.

axis0.motor.fet_thermistor.config.temp_l.doc: The lower limit when the controller starts limiting current.
The upper limit when current limit reaches 0 Amps and an over temperature error is triggered.

axis0.motor.max_allowed_current.doc:
Indicates the maximum current that can be measured by the current
sensors in the current hardware configuration. This value depends on
`config.requested_current_range`.

axis0.motor.motor_thermistor.config.temp.doc: The lower limit when the controller starts limiting current.
The upper limit when current limit reaches 0 Amps and an over temperature error is triggered.

axis0.motor.n_evt_current_measurement.doc: Number of current measurement events since startup (modulo 2^32)

axis0.motor.n_evt_pwm_update.doc: Number of PWM update events since startup (modulo 2^32)

axis0.requested_state.doc:
This is used to command the axis to change state or perform certain routines.
Values input here will be "consumed" and queued by the state machine handler.  Thus, reading this value back will usually show `UNDEFINED` (0).

axis0.steps.brief: The current commanded position, in steps, while in `step_dir` mode

axis1.acim_estimator.phase_offset.doc: estimate offset between physical and electrical angular position}

axis1.acim_estimator.rotor_flux.doc: estimated magnitude of the rotor flux

axis1.acim_estimator.slip_vel.doc: estimated slip between physical and electrical angular velocity}

axis1.acim_estimator.stator_phase.doc: calculated setpoint for the electrical phase}

axis1.acim_estimator.stator_phase_vel.doc: calculated setpoint for the electrical velocity}

axis1.config.enable_step_dir.doc:
Enable step/dir input after calibration.
Make sure to set the corresponding GPIO's mode to `GPIO_MODE_DIGITAL`.

axis1.config.startup_closed_loop_control.doc: Enable closed loop control after calibration/startup

axis1.config.startup_encoder_index_searc.doc: Run encoder index search after startup, skip otherwise this only has an effect if encoder.config.use_index is also true

axis1.config.startup_encoder_offset_cali.doc: Run encoder offset calibration after startup, skip otherwise

axis1.config.startup_motor_calibration.doc: Run motor calibration at startup, skip otherwise

axis1.config.step_dir_always_on.doc:
Keep step/dir enabled while the motor is disabled.
This is ignored if enable_step_dir is false.
This setting only takes effect on a state transition
into idle or out of closed loop control.

axis1.controller.autotuning_phase.doc: The current phase angle of the `INPUT_MODE_TUNING` sine wave generator

axis1.controller.config.axis_to_mirror.doc: The axis used for mirroring when in `INPUT_MODE_MIRROR`

axis1.controller.config.circular_setpoin.doc: circular range in [turns] for position setpoints when circular_setpoints is True

axis1.controller.config.electrical_power.doc: Bandwidth for electrical power estimate. Used for spinout detection. Dot product of Vdq and Idq

axis1.controller.config.enable_gain_sche.doc:
Enable the experimental "gain scheduling" module, which reduces the `pos_gain`, `vel_gain`, and `vel_integrator_gain` according to the position error.
Also known as "anti-hunt"

axis1.controller.config.enable_overspeed.doc: Enables the velocity controller's overspeed error

axis1.controller.config.enable_torque_mo.doc: Enable velocity limit in torque control mode (requires a valid velocity estimator).

axis1.controller.config.homing_speed.doc: The speed at which the axis moves towards the `min_endstop` during `AXIS_STATE_HOMING`

axis1.controller.config.input_filter_ban.doc: Sets the position filter's P and I gains to emulate a critically-damped 2nd order mass-spring-damper motion.

axis1.controller.config.load_encoder_axi.doc: Default depends on Axis number and is set in load_configuration()

axis1.controller.config.mechanical_power.doc: Bandwidth for mechanical power estimate. Used for spinout detection

axis1.controller.config.mirror_ratio.doc: The ratio applied to position and velocity movements of the mirrored axis.  To reverse movements, use a negative value

axis1.controller.config.spinout_electric.doc: Electrical power threshold for spinout detection. This should be a positive value

axis1.controller.config.spinout_mechanic.doc: Mechanical power threshold for spinout detection. This should be a negative value

axis1.controller.config.steps_per_circul.doc: Number of steps within the circular setpoint range. Set this and the circular setpoint range to powers of 2 for the best results.

axis1.controller.config.torque_mirror_ra.doc: The ratio applied to torque values of the mirrored axis.

axis1.controller.config.vel_integrator_l.doc: Limit the integrator output (independent of proportional gain output). Set to infinity to disable. Units = N·m

axis1.controller.input_pos.doc:
Set the desired position of the axis.  Only valid in `CONTROL_MODE_POSITION_CONTROL`.startup.
Also updates the step count.
In `INPUT_MODE_TUNING`, this acts as a DC offset for the position sine wave.

axis1.controller.input_torque.doc:
In `CONTROL_MODE_TORQUE_CONTROL`, sets the desired output torque of the axis.
In `CONTROL_MODE_VELOCITY_CONTROL` and `CONTROL_MODE_POSITION_CONTROL`, sets the feed-forward torque of the torque controller.
In `INPUT_MODE_TUNING`, this acts as a DC offset for the torque sine wave.

axis1.controller.input_vel.doc:
In `CONTROL_MODE_VELOCITY_CONTROL`, sets the desired velocity of the axis.
In `CONTROL_MODE_POSITION_CONTROL`, sets the feed-forward velocity of the velocity controller
In `INPUT_MODE_TUNING`, this acts as a DC offset for the velocity sine wave.

axis1.controller.pos_setpoint.doc: The position reference actually being used by the position controller.  This is the same as `input_pos` in `INPUT_MODE_PASSTHROUGH`, but may vary according to `InputMode`.

axis1.controller.torque_setpoint.doc: The torque reference actually being used by the torque controller.  This is the same as `input_vel` in `INPUT_MODE_PASSTHROUGH`, but may vary according to `InputMode`.

axis1.controller.trajectory_done.doc: Indicates the last commanded Trapezoidal Trajectory movement is complete.

axis1.controller.vel_integrator_torque.doc: The accumulated value of the velocity loop integrator

axis1.controller.vel_setpoint.doc: The velocity reference actually being used by the velocity controller.  This is the same as `input_vel` in `INPUT_MODE_PASSTHROUGH`, but may vary according to `InputMode`.

axis1.current_state.brief: The current state of the axis

axis1.encoder.config.abs_spi_cs_gpio_pin.doc: Make sure that the GPIO is in `GPIO_MODE_DIGITAL`.

axis1.encoder.config.calib_range.doc: The error threshold for encoder offset calibration, in turns.  If the

axis1.encoder.config.calib_scan_distance.doc:
The distance the motor is turned during encoder offset calibration.
This is in the electrical frame, so if you want a 7pp motor to turn 1 mechanical revolution, you would put `(7 * 2*pi)`

axis1.encoder.config.calib_scan_omega.doc:
The speed the motor turns during encoder offset calibration.
This is in the electrical frame, so a 7pp motor rotating 1 mechanical revolution in 2 sec would be set to `(7 * 2*pi) / 2`

axis1.encoder.config.cpr.doc: Counts per Revolution of the encoder.  This is 4x the Pulses per Revolution.

axis1.encoder.config.index_offset.doc: When the index is found, the linear position of the axis will be set to this value if `use_index_offset` is set to `True`.

axis1.encoder.config.sincos_gpio_pin_cos.doc: Analog cosine signal of a sin/cos encoder. The corresponding GPIO must be in `GPIO_MODE_ANALOG_IN`.

axis1.encoder.config.sincos_gpio_pin_sin.doc: Analog sine signal of a sin/cos encoder. The corresponding GPIO must be in `GPIO_MODE_ANALOG_IN`.

axis1.encoder.config.use_index.doc: Set this to `True` when using an encoder with an index pin to allow pre-calibration of the encoder and encoder index search.

axis1.encoder.config.use_index_offset.doc: Set this to `True` to have the axis set the linear position of the axis to `index_offset` when the index is found during encoder index search

axis1.encoder.count_in_cpr.doc: Raw circular count from the encoder on [0, cpr)

axis1.encoder.delta_pos_cpr_counts.doc: Circular position delta of the encoder in the most recent loop. Primarily for debug purposes, it indicates much the encoder changed since the last time it was checked.

axis1.encoder.pos_abs.doc: The last (valid) position from an absolute encoder, if used.

axis1.encoder.pos_circular.doc: Circular position estimate of the encoder, as a decimal from [0, 1).  Also known as "single-turn" position.

axis1.encoder.pos_cpr_counts.doc: Circular position estimate of the encoder, on the space [0, cpr).

axis1.encoder.pos_estimate.doc: Linear position estimate of the encoder, in turns.  Also known as "multi-turn" position.

axis1.encoder.pos_estimate_counts.doc: Linear position estimate of the encoder, in counts.  Equal to `pos_estimate * config.cpr`

axis1.encoder.shadow_count.doc: Raw linear count from the encoder.

axis1.encoder.vel_estimate.doc: Estimate of the linear velocity of an axis in turn/s

axis1.encoder.vel_estimate_counts.doc: Estimate of the linear velocity of an axis, in counts/s.

axis1.is_homed.brief: Whether or not the axis has been successfully homed.

axis1.max_endstop.config.gpio_num.doc: Make sure the corresponding GPIO is in `GPIO_MODE_DIGITAL`.

axis1.min_endstop.config.gpio_num.doc: Make sure the corresponding GPIO is in `GPIO_MODE_DIGITAL`.

axis1.motor.I_bus.doc: The current in the ODrive DC bus.  This is also the current seen by the power supply in most systems.

axis1.motor.config.I_bus_hard_max.doc:
If the controller fails to keep this motor's DC current (`ODrive.Motor:I_bus`)
below this value the motor gets disarmed immediately. Usually this
is set in conjunction with `I_bus_hard_min`. Set to inf to disable.
Take noise into account when chosing a value.

axis1.motor.config.I_bus_hard_min.doc:
If the controller fails to keep this motor's DC current (`ODrive.Motor:I_bus`)
above this value the motor gets disarmed immediately. Most likely
you want a negative value here. Set to -inf to disable. Take noise
into account when chosing a value.

axis1.motor.config.I_leak_max.doc:
In almost all scenarios, the currents on phase A, B and C should
add up to zero. A small amount of measurement noise is expected.
However if the sum of A, B, C currents exceeds this configuration
value, the motor gets disarmed immediately.

Note that this feature is only works on devices with three current
sensors (e.g. ODrive v4).

axis1.motor.config.R_wL_FF_enable.doc: Enables automatic feedforward of the R*wL term in the current controller.

axis1.motor.config.bEMF_FF_enable.doc: Enables automatic feedforward of the bEMF term in the current controller.

axis1.motor.config.calibration_current.doc: The current used to measure resistance during `AXIS_STATE_MOTOR_CALIBRATION`.

axis1.motor.config.current_control_bandw.doc:
Sets the PI gains of the Q and D axis FOC control according to `phase_resistance` and `phase_inductance` to create a critically-damped controller with a -3dB
bandwidth at this frequency.

axis1.motor.config.current_lim_margin.doc: Maximum measured current allowed above `current_lim`.  Any value above `current_lim + curren_lim_margin` will throw a `CURRENT_LIMIT_VIOLATION` error.

axis1.motor.config.pole_pairs.doc:
The number of pole pairs in the motor.
Note this is equal to 1/2 of the number of magnets (not coils!) in a typical hobby motor.

axis1.motor.config.pre_calibrated.doc:
Indicates to the ODrive that the parameters `config.phase_resistance` and `config.phase_inductance` are valid at system start.
If these are valid and `pre_calibrated` is set to `True`, motor calibration can be skipped.

axis1.motor.config.requested_current_ran.doc:
The minimum phase current range expected to be measured.  This is used to set the current shunt amplifier gains.
This should be set > `current_lim + curren_lim_margin`, but as low as possible to maximize precision and accuracy of the controller.

axis1.motor.config.resistance_calib_max_.doc:
The maximum voltage allowed during `AXIS_STATE_MOTOR_CALIBRATION`.
This should be set to less than `(0.5 * vbus_voltage)`, but high enough to satisfy V=IR during motor calibration, where I is `config.calibration_current` and R is `config.phase_resistance`

axis1.motor.config.torque_lim.doc: Maximum commanded torque allowed in the torque loop.

axis1.motor.current_control.Id_measured.doc: The phase current measured along the "d" axis in the FOC control loop.  This should be close to 0 for typical surface permanent magnet motors.

axis1.motor.current_control.Iq_measured.doc: The phase current measured along the "q" axis in the FOC control loop.  This is the torque-generating current, so motor torque is approx. `torque_constant * Iq_measured`

axis1.motor.current_control.power.doc: The electrical power being delivered to the motor

axis1.motor.effective_current_lim.doc: This value is the internally-limited value of phase current allowed according to the set current limit and the FET and Motor thermistor limits.

axis1.motor.fet_thermistor.config.temp_l.doc: The lower limit when the controller starts limiting current.
The upper limit when current limit reaches 0 Amps and an over temperature error is triggered.

axis1.motor.max_allowed_current.doc:
Indicates the maximum current that can be measured by the current
sensors in the current hardware configuration. This value depends on
`config.requested_current_range`.

axis1.motor.motor_thermistor.config.temp.doc: The lower limit when the controller starts limiting current.
The upper limit when current limit reaches 0 Amps and an over temperature error is triggered.

axis1.motor.n_evt_current_measurement.doc: Number of current measurement events since startup (modulo 2^32)

axis1.motor.n_evt_pwm_update.doc: Number of PWM update events since startup (modulo 2^32)

axis1.requested_state.doc:
This is used to command the axis to change state or perform certain routines.
Values input here will be "consumed" and queued by the state machine handler.  Thus, reading this value back will usually show `UNDEFINED` (0).

axis1.steps.brief: The current commanded position, in steps, while in `step_dir` mode

config.brake_resistance.brief: Value of the brake resistor connected to the ODrive.
config.brake_resistance.doc:
If you set this to a lower value than the true brake resistance
then the ODrive will not meed the `max_regen_current` constraint
during braking, that is it will sink more than `max_regen_current`
into the power supply. Some power supplies don't like this.

If you set this to a higher value than the true brake resistance
then the ODrive will unnecessarily burn more power than required
during braking.

config.dc_bus_overvoltage_ramp_end.doc: Must be larger than `dc_bus_overvoltage_ramp_start`, otherwise the ramp feature is disabled.

config.dc_bus_overvoltage_ramp_start.doc: Do not set this lower than your usual `ODrive:vbus_voltage`, unless you like fried brake resistors.

config.dc_bus_overvoltage_trip_level.brief: Maximum voltage above which the motor stops operating.
config.dc_bus_overvoltage_trip_level.doc:
This protects against cases in which the power supply fails to dissipate
the brake power if the brake resistor is disabled.
The default is 26V for the 24V board version and 52V for the 48V board version.

config.dc_bus_undervoltage_trip_level.brief: Minimum voltage below which the motor stops operating.

config.dc_max_negative_current.brief: Max current the power supply can sink.
config.dc_max_negative_current.doc:
You most likely want a non-positive value here. Set to -INFINITY to disable.
Note: This should be greater in magnitude than `max_regen_current`

config.dc_max_positive_current.brief: Max current the power supply can source.

config.enable_brake_resistor.brief: Enable/disable the use of a brake resistor.
config.enable_brake_resistor.doc:
Setting this to False even though a brake resistor is connected is
harmless. Setting this to True even though no brake resistor is
connected can break the power supply.
Changes to this value require a reboot to take effect.

config.enable_can_a.doc: Enables CAN. Changing this setting requires a reboot.

config.enable_dc_bus_overvoltage_ramp.brief: Enables the DC bus overvoltage ramp feature.
config.enable_dc_bus_overvoltage_ramp.doc:
If enabled, if the measured DC voltage exceeds `dc_bus_overvoltage_ramp_start`,
the ODrive will sink more power than usual into the the brake resistor
in an attempt to bring the voltage down again.

The brake duty cycle is increased by the following amount:

 * `ODrive:vbus_voltage` == `dc_bus_overvoltage_ramp_start`  =>  brake_duty_cycle += 0%
 * `ODrive:vbus_voltage` == `dc_bus_overvoltage_ramp_end`  =>  brake_duty_cycle += 100%

Remarks:
 - This feature is active even when all motors are disarmed.
 - This feature is disabled if `brake_resistance` is non-positive.

config.enable_i2c_a.doc:
Enables I2C. The I2C pins on ODrive v3.x are in conflict with CAN.
This setting has no effect if `enable_can_a` is also true.
This setting has no effect on ODrive v3.2 or earlier.
Changing this setting requires a reboot.

config.enable_uart_a.doc:
You also need to set the corresponding GPIOs to GPIO_MODE_UART_A.
Refer to [interfaces](interfaces.md) to see which pins support UART_A.
Changing this requires a reboot.

config.enable_uart_b.doc:
You also need to set the corresponding GPIOs to GPIO_MODE_UART_B.
Refer to [interfaces](interfaces.md) to see which pins support UART_B.
Changing this requires a reboot.

config.gpio10_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO10 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio11_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO11 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio12_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO12 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio13_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO13 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio14_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO14 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio15_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO15 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio16_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO16 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio1_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO1 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio2_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO2 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio3_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO3 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio4_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO4 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio5_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO5 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio6_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO6 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio7_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO7 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio8_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO8 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.gpio9_mode.doc: Mode of GPIO9 (changes take effect after reboot)

config.max_regen_current.doc: The bus current allowed to flow back to the power supply before the brake resistor module will start shunting current.

config.uart_a_baudrate.brief: Defines the baudrate used on the UART interface.

config.uart_b_baudrate.brief: Defines the baudrate used on the UART interface.

config.usb_cdc_protocol.doc:
The protocol that's being run on the device's virtual COM port on
USB.
Note that the ODrive has two independent interfaces on USB: One
is the virtual COM port (affected by this option) and the other
one is a vendor specific interface which always runs Fibre.
So changing this option does not affect the working of odrivetool.

ibus.brief: Current on the DC bus as calculated by the ODrive.
ibus.doc:
A positive value means that the ODrive is consuming power from the power supply,
a negative value means that the ODrive is sourcing power to the power supply.

This value is equal to the sum of the motor currents and the brake resistor currents.
The motor currents are measured, the brake resistor current is calculated based on
`config.brake_resistance`.

ibus_report_filter_k.doc:
Filter gain for the reported `ibus`. Set to a value below 1.0 to get a smoother
line when plotting `ibus`. Set to 1.0 to disable. This filter is only applied to
the reported value and not for internal calculations.

misconfigured.doc:
If this property is true, something is bad in the configuration. The
ODrive can still be used in this state but the user should investigate
which setting is problematic. This variable does not cover all
misconfigurations.

Possible causes:
 - A GPIO was set to a mode that it doesn't support
 - A GPIO was set to a mode for which the corresponding feature was
   not enabled. Example: `GPIO_MODE_UART_A` was used without enabling
   `config.enable_uart_a`.
 - A feature was enabled which is not supported on this hardware.
   Example: `config.enable_uart_c` set to true on ODrive v3.x.
 - A GPIO was used as an interrupt input for two internal components
   or two GPIOs that are mutually exclusive in their interrupt
   capability were both used as interrupt input.
   Example: `Axis:config.step_gpio_pin` of both axes were set to the same GPIO.

n_evt_control_loop.doc: Number of control loop iterations since startup (modulo 2^32)

n_evt_sampling.doc: Number of input sampling events since startup (modulo 2^32)

task_timers_armed.doc:
Set by a profiling application to trigger sampling of a single
control iteration. Cleared by the device as soon as the sampling
is complete.

vbus_voltage.brief: Voltage on the DC bus as measured by the ODrive.
